title: Integral compact supports have the prescribed reductions
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], so $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ has characteristic $p$. Fix $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_n=R/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Integral coefficients on a scheme $T$ mean modules over $\widehat R_T=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_T$ on the small pro-étale site, not over the discrete constant sheaf $R$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients].

Let $X,Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type morphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Let $d\geq0$ be an integer with $\dim X\leq d$ [def-kun-dimension]. Let $a\leq b$ be integers and $K\in D^b_c(X,R)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Suppose that every derived reduction $K_n=K\otimes_R^L A_n$ [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction] has Tor amplitude in the same interval $[a,b]$, in the intrinsic sense of [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. For the integral and finite-level compact-support functors defined in [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], one has

$$
Rf_!K\in D^b_c(Y,R),\qquad
(Rf_!K)\otimes_R^L A_n\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{!,n}K_n\quad(n\geq1).
$$

Every displayed reduction has Tor amplitude in $[a,b+2d]$. The displayed isomorphisms are the canonical compact-support coefficient comparisons, compatible with successive reductions.

proof.text: The finite-field characteristic is p, so ell different from p is a unit in k: apply charP_of_card_eq_prime_pow to the finite base field and map the resulting unit into its algebraic closure. Apply the existing sfIntegralCompactSupport_constructible theorem to the supplied Roos triangle to obtain integral constructibility of M. This theorem concerns exactly sfCompactSupportTerm and sfCompactSupportTransition, with the fixed compactification c.

proof.text: Take the very chosen derived limit N and projection q used by sfIntegralCompactSupportValue and sfCompactSupportChosenReduction. Complete the identity morphisms on the two product vertices to a morphism from the supplied distinguished triangle to that chosen triangle. The two-isomorphisms theorem makes its first component v:M to N invertible, and the first triangle square gives v followed by q equal to p. Naturality of the scalar-extension/restriction adjunction identifies the adjunct of p followed by the nth projection with scalar extension of v followed by sfCompactSupportChosenReduction. The existing sfCompactSupportChosenReduction_isIso therefore proves invertibility of every specified comparison, preserving the actual projections.

proof.text: For the finite-level bound use c.denseRefinement, with its natural structure map to Spec k. Its proper map is finite type, and its open immersion is quasi-compact and scheme-theoretically dominant, hence has dense topological range. The dimension-extension theorem identifies the dimension of its ambient scheme with dim X, so it is at most d.

proof.text: Integral constructibility of K supplies intrinsic bounded constructibility at each positive reduction. Extension by zero along the dense-refinement open preserves constructibility and the exact interval [a,b]. Apply finiteCoefficientDirectImage_boundedConstructible_torAmplitude to its proper map over the fixed finite-field datum, with the ambient dimension bound d. This gives [a,b+2d] for the dense-refinement compact-support image.

proof.text: Use finiteRing_constructibleDerived_origin to lift each bounded constructible reduction to a bounded constructible etale complex. The bounded-below condition follows from its cohomological interval. Transport compact support through sfIntrinsicDerivedEquivalence, using the counit of the underived realization equivalence for open extension and sfIntrinsicDerivedDirectImageComparison for proper direct image. Apply the existing pro-etale/etale compact-support comparison and the existing etale compactification independence isomorphism rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactificationPlusιIso. Their composite identifies the dense-refinement output with the original fixed-c output. The intrinsic Tor condition is invariant under this isomorphism: compose each cochain representative isomorphism with its inverse. Finally transport along the inverse of the already proved projection adjunct to obtain the stated Tor bound on the reduction of M.

proof.text: The first two morphisms of the supplied distinguished Roos triangle compose to zero. Expand the second morphism as identity minus towerProductShift and compose with the nth product projection. Additivity and the product projection equations give p followed by projection n+1 followed by the transition equal to p followed by projection n. This uses only the distinguished-triangle zero-composition lemma and the definition of the tower shift.

proof.text: Apply injectivity of the higher scalar-extension/restriction adjunction homEquiv to the required successive-reduction equation. Naturality in its right variable converts each side to the underlying projection. Naturality of sfCompactSupportDerivedRestrictionComp.inv moves the lower comparison across the composite-restriction identification. The lower adjunction unit identity identifies that composite with p followed by projection n. Cancel the invertible composite-restriction comparison and use the projection transition equation from the preceding step. This proves compatibility of the actual adjunct maps, independently of any choice of transition representatives.
